subject: Streaming glitch: remediation plan & customer guidance
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>, Sasha Li <sasha.li@bridgebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming glitch impacting Finova chat sessions — immediate mitigations

Alex / Sasha —

I’m really sorry for the disruption this morning. Our monitoring flagged elevated tail latency on streaming/chat endpoints affecting a subset of Finova sessions starting ~08:50 PST; you may have seen messages stall or arrive in multi-second chunks.

What we’ve done so far (immediate):
- Scoped traffic: we routed Finova requests away from the impacted edge shard at 09:00 PST.
- Temporary fallback: enabled the non-streaming (complete response) path for affected requests for customers who requested it.
- Telemetry capture: collected KV cache timelines and socket traces; attaching a condensed timeline (incident-timelines.csv).

Quick mitigations you can apply client-side right now (low friction):
- Retry on stalled stream: if your client sees no tokens for >1s, re-open the websocket once; in practice we’ve seen successful resumed streams on a single reconnect.
- Short-poll fallback: configure a short-poll (1s) to hit the non-streaming endpoint for critical user flows if you need guaranteed delivery.
- Reduce chunk size: if you send multi-turn prompts with long system/context tokens, try trimming non-essential context for the next 24 hours.

We’re preparing a short remediation plan and will share a timeline for a permanent fix shortly. I’ll set aside time this afternoon to walk through the timeline with you and propose a credit for the affected window.

Attachments: incident-timelines.csv (CSV)

—
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>, Sasha Li <sasha.li@bridgebank.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Streaming glitch impacting Finova chat sessions — immediate mitigations

Eve —

Thanks for the heads-up and the initial customer-facing note. Quick technical summary from infra:
- Root cause (prelim): a coordinated cache-eviction pattern on one edge shard caused KV cache misses at token-emission time, which cascaded to our batching controller and increased tail latency for streaming connections.
- Scope: ~7% of streaming connections in us-west-2 region between 08:50–09:25 PST, concentrated on longer context sessions (>1k tokens).
- Short-term remediation applied: we blackholed the problematic shard at 09:00 PST and forced sticky routing to adjacent healthy shards; that reduced new occurrences immediately.

Recommended next steps (action items):
1) Push a hotfix to the batching controller to add a small grace window for KV-cache rewarm (Marissa -> infra team; target EOD).
2) Coordinate a config change to reduce default streaming batch size from 4 -> 2 for high-context workloads for 48 hours (Ben -> runtime).
3) Draft an internal postmortem and an external remediation note with suggested SDK retries + sample code (Eve -> customer comms).

I attached a condensed timeline and basic metrics. If Alex/Sasha want an immediate rollback to fully non-streaming for all users, we can flip that but it will increase token cost and latency slightly; recommend only for isolated premium flows.

Attachments: incident-timelines.csv

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Li <sasha.li@bridgebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Streaming glitch impacting Finova chat sessions — immediate mitigations

Thanks Evelyn — and thanks Marissa for the breakdown. A few quick questions from our side: 
1) What’s the expected timeline for the hotfix? Our SREs want a firm ETA so we can plan the weekend runbook.
2) For the quick client-side guidance: can you send a small code snippet for the recommended reconnect behavior? We need something our frontend team can drop in.
3) Will there be a credit or SLA remediation for the impacted window? We had a number of interrupted support chats this morning.

We appreciate the fast response.

—
Alex Turner
Head of Product Operations, Finova
alex.turner@finova.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>, Sasha Li <sasha.li@bridgebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Streaming glitch impacting Finova chat sessions — remediation plan, timeline, and next steps

Alex / Sasha —

Thank you for the questions and for your patience today. Below is a concise remediation timeline and customer-facing post-incident plan.

Post-incident summary (TL;DR):
- Incident window: 2027-01-09 08:50–09:25 PST.
- Impact: ~7% of streaming sessions in us-west-2; main symptom = delayed/missing token emission and multi-second chunking.
- Root cause (prelim): cache-eviction spike on a single edge shard causing KV cache miss storms and batching controller queuing.

Actions & timeline: 
- 09:00 PST: traffic routed away from affected shard (complete).
- 11:00 PST: runtime team deployed a temporary config to reduce streaming batch size (4 -> 2) for high-context requests.
- 17:00 PST (EOD): infra will ship a hotfix to batching controller that adds a 500ms KV-rewarm grace window (target).
- By 2027-01-11: scheduled deploy of a tuned cache rewarm heuristic (permanent fix).

Customer guidance (what to do now):
- Client reconnect snippet (JS websockets):
  if (noTokensReceivedForMillis > 1000) {
    ws.close();
    setTimeout(() => openNewConnection(), 250); // single reconnect attempt recommended
  }
- Non-streaming fallback: call /v1/generate for critical flows when consistent delivery is required.
- Context trimming: reduce prompt context for sessions that exceed 1k tokens for the next 48 hours.

Credit / SLA: we’ll propose a one-time credit for the affected window and will follow up with an exact credit calculation by Monday. I’ve looped in CS for formal quote.

Next steps (we will):
- Share a finalized external incident summary by Monday AM (Evelyn).
- Schedule a 30-minute postmortem review with Finova and our runtime team (please pick times here: https://cal.redwood.com/evelyn/30min).
- Provide the final hotfix PR and test notes to your SREs before the permanent rollout.

Attachments: ev-to-customer-20270109-remediation.pdf (one-page customer summary)

Again, apologies for the disruption — we’re committed to making this right and ensuring you have reliable streaming going forward.

—
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
